flashcard_questions.q: What share of global energy production still comes from non-renewable sources?
What makes an energy source renewable?
flashcard_questions.a: It can be used indefinitely without running out.

flashcard_questions.q: How does loft insulation cut a household's energy use?
flashcard_questions.a: It stops heat escaping through the roof, so less heating is needed.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can Nepal not rely on fossil fuels?
flashcard_questions.a: It has no reserves of its own and cannot afford large imports.

flashcard_questions.q: What environmental damage does Nepal's use of wood fuel cause?
flashcard_questions.a: Deforestation, which reduces biodiversity and raises flood risk.
Small-scale electricity generation from water channelled downhill through a turbine.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is Nepal so rich in water resources?
flashcard_questions.a: Its mountains carry rivers fed by Himalayan snowmelt.

flashcard_questions.q: How many people could Nepal's water resources supply with electricity?
Why is micro-hydro preferred to a large hydroelectric dam in Nepal?
flashcard_questions.a: It is cheaper and quicker to build, and it serves the local village directly.

flashcard_questions.q: How many micro-hydro plants has the UNDP helped build in Nepal?
How many people do those UNDP micro-hydro plants supply?
Why does the UNDP train villagers to run the micro-hydro plants?
flashcard_questions.a: So communities can maintain them and build more without outside help.

flashcard_questions.q: What happened to the noodle factory in Karbang once electricity arrived?
flashcard_questions.a: It tripled its production and created new products.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can more Nepalese children attend school after micro-hydro arrives?
flashcard_questions.a: Families no longer need them to collect firewood all day.

flashcard_questions.q: Which renewable device in Nepal turns animal waste into fuel?

notes: 15 cards: 3 term-to-definition (renewable, micro-hydro, biogas digester), 4 case-study-to-fact with one figure each (87% non-renewable, 27 million people, 400 plants, 500,000 supplied), 6 cause-to-consequence (fossil fuel position, wood fuel damage, snowmelt, micro-hydro over dams, UNDP training, children in school), 2 strategy-to-example (loft insulation, Karbang noodle factory).
